## TL;DR

Extended release email rendering with grouped Features, Fixes, and Other sections, repository-host-aware release and changelog links, and one-use recipient unsubscribe links. Unsubscribe tokens and suppressed addresses live in a local cache file; the public endpoint consumes a token and prevents that address from receiving later release email. The focused release-email tests passed, and the scoped RepoOS check passed after formatting.

## Work and rationale

The renderer already owned the HTML and text templates, so grouping was implemented there without adding a mail dependency or changing the delivery provider. The section mapper uses familiar release-note headings: headings containing feature/new/added classify following content as Features; fix/bug/repair classify it as Fixes; remaining content goes under Other. Empty sections stay out of the email, and an entirely empty notes body keeps the existing empty-state copy. Text output follows the same grouping so recipients who read plain text get equivalent organization.

Repository configuration previously accepted only an `owner/repo` string and the renderer constructed GitHub URLs directly. The renderer now also accepts an explicit HTTP or HTTPS repository URL. For GitHub it preserves the established `/releases/tag/` and `/blob/` patterns; other hosts use the common `/-/releases/tag/` and `/-/blob/` routes. Unsupported schemes and malformed values produce no repository links rather than unsafe URLs. This treats `release.repository` as a web location for rendering; the existing GitHub-only publish readiness probe remains unchanged.

Unsubscribe state is stored under the configured cache directory in `release-email-unsubscribes.json`, separate from per-release send records. Every recipient gets a cryptographically random token associated with their address. The public GET handler consumes that token once, records the address in the suppression list, and returns a small confirmation page. The route is explicitly public because email recipients do not have RepoOS sessions. Sending filters suppressed recipients before attempting delivery. Outgoing messages resolve their origin through the existing RepoOS `webOrigin` helper, which supports an explicit public URL, a request origin, or a configured tunnel; the individual resend route also supplies its request origin.

## Approaches tried

I first considered deriving unsubscribe links from the repository URL, but that URL identifies a source host, not the running RepoOS instance. I used the shared `webOrigin` resolver instead so generated links point back to the application. Tokens are random and single-use rather than embedding an address in a query string. Tests use temporary roots, fake addresses, a fake Resend key, and the existing fake network seams; no test sends an external email.

## Challenges and blockers

The first focused test run caught malformed regex literals introduced while trimming URL slashes. Those were replaced with explicit `endsWith` handling. A route test uses a minimal request object without headers, so origin resolution now safely falls back to localhost in that case. The first remote scoped gate encountered a timeout in the unrelated host-pressure recovery test; a subsequent run passed all 126 scoped test files. The gate then identified formatting drift, which I fixed with the repository formatter, and the final scoped check passed including build, tests, contrast audit, and UI smoke.

## Key learnings

Release note grouping must be applied to content as it is read, not just section labels, so bullets after a heading remain in that category until the next heading. Email unsubscribe URLs need both a stable recipient mapping and the application’s public origin; the repository host cannot stand in for the app host. Reusing shared origin resolution keeps email links consistent with other RepoOS notifications. Finally, the release publishing probe and the release page URL serve different purposes: supporting links for another git host does not require changing the existing GitHub publication check.
